publications.benefit: Clean up temporary release directories and archives after failed standalone downloads and extraction, preserving original exit statuses and the previous executable.
publications.scope: One installer function, scoped Bash subshell EXIT trap and two regression cases.
publications.limits: Synthetic release bytes and stub Docker. Hosted releases and Windows not exercised. Upstream CI separate.
tests: Two baseline failures and two passing controls.
34 installer/update tests passed on macOS with Bash 3.2.57.
Offline Ubuntu with Bash 5.0.17: success and both failure cases pass with native mktemp.
Bash syntax, Ruff and diff checks pass; ShellCheck has zero added and one fewer finding.

publications.benefit: Keep the full viewer/TUI transcript readable when persisted or live SDK tool text would parse into a non-finite JSON number.
publications.scope: One shared projection parser with finite checks for constants and floats; fallback keeps original text, finite JSON structure and durable SDK history.
publications.limits: Synthetic SDK tool output through real SQLite, HTTP and TUI encoder. No live model, service, scan, Windows or visual client interaction.
tests: Eight regressions failed on unchanged main and 12 controls passed. All 20 passed after the patch.
163 focused TUI/viewer tests passed with the frozen lock on macOS Python 3.12.14.
Actual HTTP/encoder probe switched four invalid outputs to valid JavaScript JSON.parse results; two controls still pass.
Global Ruff, Mypy (137 files) and Bandit passed. Pyright reported 945 pre-existing diagnostics with zero changes after normalization.

issue_only.benefit: Prevent an operator from treating timed-out steering as a definitive failure and sending a duplicate command.
issue_only.scope: Maintainer decision on cancellation before acceptance versus unknown delivery and retry identity after acceptance. No code.
issue_only.limits: Synthetic local run using the real coordinator and TUI event loop; no LLM, scan or live web UI. A late snapshot causing a similar problem was inferred by inspection.
tests: A real 10-second wait reported not_delivered; after the loop resumed the first message was queued, and retry queued an identical second message.

issue_only.benefit: Separate an accepted top-up request from a valid credit receipt, without encouraging a possibly duplicate payment.
issue_only.scope: Maintainer decision on recovery/wording for an unverified receipt. Public OpenAPI specifies four required fields even for duplicate receipts. No code.
issue_only.limits: Local Requests with a synthetic transport. No evidence that the real service sends an invalid response, no wallet subprocess, real API or transaction.
tests: Three malformed HTTP 200 receipts incorrectly exit 0; both complete controls including the duplicate pass with one synthetic POST each.

usestrix/strix#pr:1401.note: The author withdrew the conflicted branch and is no longer pursuing it. The observed head is unchanged and is an ancestor of fork master 1.2.50 through 34f7f98a. Both sync and async completion guards are present in delivered code. All 30 tests in the release source cost-tracking suite passed, including real LiteLLM callbacks with synthetic transport. The current upstream tree does not carry those guards. Keep the existing fork implementation.

usestrix/strix#pr:1428.note: Dependabot closed its earlier viewer dependency group because the dependencies can be updated another way. #1721 is the current grouped viewer proposal. No selected backport.

usestrix/strix#pr:1643.note: Dependabot closed its earlier Python dependency group because the dependencies can be updated another way. #1722 is the current grouped Python proposal. No selected backport.

usestrix/strix#pr:1691.note: The updated head clarifies what the log limit opt-out restores. Active documentation PR. No competing edit.

usestrix/strix#pr:1699.note: Active separate proposal for not_reached terminology/usage level. #1701 merged per-CVE reachability and neutral wording with a same-series skill revert. Keep this proposal separate.

usestrix/strix#pr:1701.note: Merged at e0594808 after maintainer approval. Per-CVE reachability verdict and neutral not_applicable wording remain; the later loaded-package rule was reverted in the same series. Current reporting tests were included in the 232 passing MCP/reporting cases. Fork has independent reporting changes; compare semantics before importing.

usestrix/strix#pr:1702.note: Existing active NSS CA idempotence work. State and head unchanged. It does not establish the cause of the readiness issue reported in #1704. No overlapping proposal.

usestrix/strix#issue:1704.note: New participant traced current startup and requested a sanitized readiness/output probe; they could not reproduce corrupted output or establish the cause. #1053 and fork #47 concern an earlier Caido guest-login deadline. Await a controlled before/after readiness reproduction before changing startup or decoding.

usestrix/strix#issue:1709.note: Another contributor opened #1714 for the target-loss report. Its regression sends both distinct target frames before setup.start. The exact two PR diffs #1713 and #1714 apply together to e0594808; all 119 app Go race tests pass including that regression. The test establishes local frame ordering while acknowledgements are withheld, not the behavior of a backend rejection.
usestrix/strix#issue:1709.revisit: After #1714 merges, verify the final target sequence and separately examine behavior when the backend rejects an addition.

usestrix/strix#pr:1714.note: Payload-specific pending keys keep separate target additions in flight, while repeated identical payloads still collide. Updated regression asserts that setup.start is sent after both targets. 119 app Go race tests pass on e0594808 with the full #1713 and #1714 diffs. This is an independent contributor proposal. Backend rejection remains a separate contract question.

usestrix/strix#issue:1715.note: The author closed the request as completed. The visible timeline provides no resolving commit or rationale. Solution presence and behavior were not established on fork master, so do not mark it resolved in the fork.

usestrix/strix#pr:1716.note: Closed without merge and without an explicit closure rationale in the reviewed timeline. #1717 carries the same initial bearer refresh approach and resolves the two bot findings by propagating the eager refresher and sharing failed concurrent refresh attempts.

usestrix/strix#pr:1717.note: Merged at 18fa4c84. The optional HTTP MCP refresher retries a 401 with a new bearer and preserves refresh attempt generation for concurrent failures. 232 focused MCP/auth/client/resilience/reporting tests pass on the resulting main. Fork master has no new auth module; evaluate its registry and refresh integration separately.

usestrix/strix#pr:1719.note: Existing implementation for the Herdr workspace request. Defer any overlapping integration pending upstream review.

usestrix/strix#issue:1718.note: Active Herdr integration proposal #1719 already implements the request. Do not duplicate it.

usestrix/strix#pr:1680.note: Unchanged open head. Corrupt UTF-8 in the auth record remains reproducible and this proposed diff omits the reader. The PR is already widening tolerant state/auth reads. Avoid competing scope pending its outcome.
